name: UBC Summer Science Program for Indigenous students
org: UBC Centre for Excellence in Indigenous Health, Faculty of Medicine
what_you_do: Spend one week on the UBC campus. You do cultural, health and science workshops. Examples are drum-making, a virtual reality medicine lab and Talking Circles led by Elders. You also meet Indigenous mentors in health and science.
who_can_apply: First Nations, Inuit or Metis students going into grades 9 to 12. Week 1 is for students going into grades 11 or 12. Week 2 is for students going into grades 9 or 10. The pages do not state an age rule.
pay_detail: $200 program fee covers housing and meals. Workshops and Vancouver Aquarium admission are covered. Bursaries for students with financial need and travel bursaries are available. Travel to Vancouver is not included.
deadline_text: The 2026 application deadline was June 15, 2026. The program page for 2025 listed Week 1 as Aug 3 to 9 and Week 2 as Aug 10 to 16, with applications closing June 1. 2027 dates are not posted.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Summer Science application online (UBC form). Or send it by email to summer.science@ubc.ca, or by mail. A reference letter of about 200 words is recommended. It can come from a teacher, coach, mentor or community leader.
notes: Only for Indigenous students (First Nations, Inuit, Metis). It is a camp, not a job. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them. The program page still shows 2025 dates, so check the newest page before you plan. The application page lists the 2026 deadline of June 15, 2026.
